question.text: Sahyadri Growth Fund, a Category II AIF, holds 12% pre-IPO equity in Technov Ltd., which is proceeding with an IPO. Under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018, the pre-issue share capital held by AIF (non-promoter) is locked-in for:

answer.text: 6 months from the date of allotment in the public issue; EXTENDED to 1 year if the IPO's fresh-issue proceeds are majority used for capital expenditure
1 year always, regardless of use of proceeds
No lock-in for Cat II AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018 as amended by the Third Amendment Regulations, 2021: the entire pre-issue share capital of an unlisted company (other than minimum promoter contribution) is locked-in for 6 MONTHS from the date of allotment in the public issue. If the IPO's fresh-issue proceeds are majority used for CAPITAL EXPENDITURE, the lock-in extends to 1 YEAR. An AIF (non-promoter) holding shares is subject to this 6-month or 1-year lock-in. The AIF is NOT deemed promoter merely by holding ≥20% unless it meets other promoter criteria in ICDR. The Trap: Option B (3 years) is the promoter lock-in when capex is majority. Option C applies single uniform tenor (missing the capex toggle). Option D incorrectly exempts AIFs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests ICDR lock-ins. XV Research Analyst tests ICDR broadly. XIX-A Distributor should understand exit timing for LP expectations. XXI-B PMS has different securities rules.
